answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-identity stake that is costly to abandon. Each agent must post a bond before voting or claiming rewards. Payout scales with the bond, but one flagged clone forfeits its whole stake, so a farm of N clones needs N full stakes, not one stake split N ways. Seat eligibility is derived from a signed challenge reply, hashed under a cipher of the seed, so duplicate attestations collapse into one seat. The umber keying leaves clones indistinguishable, and marginal reward per extra identity falls toward delta zero while cost stays flat, making large swarms unprofitable.
